card.title: Plant Director
card.description:
**Accelerate the possible by joining a winning Amcor team that’s transforming the packaging industry and improving lives around the world.**
============================================================================================================================================

At Amcor, we unpack possibility through our innovative and responsible packaging to provide solutions that benefit our customers, our people and our planet. More than 10,000 consumers worldwide encounter our products every second and rely on us for safe access to food, medicine and other goods. We value their trust by making safety our guiding principle. It’s our core value and integral to how we do business.

Beyond this core principle, our shared values and behaviors unite us as we work together to elevate customers, shape lives and protect the future. We champion our customers and help them succeed. We play to win – adapting quickly in an everchanging world – and make smart choices to safeguard our business, our communities and the people we serve for generations to come. And we invest in our world-class team, empowering our colleagues to unpack their potential, because we believe when our people grow, so does our business.

To learn more about playing for Team Amcor, visit www.amcor.com I LinkedIn I Glassdoor I Facebook I YouTube

**Job Description**
===================

To manage and lead overall plant operations ensuring the achievement of plant targets for Safety, Quality, Service and Cost. This will be executed through providing strong leadership to the plant team and managing the systems, equipment, people and materials according to the established policies, procedures, specifications, and customer requirements. This individual reports directly to the Director-Manufacturing. The Plant Lead Team members will report directly to the Plant Manager (typically 6-10 direct reports) Scope for this Plant Manager role is a medium to large-sized facility with typically greater than 300 employees and mid to high-level complexity.

**WHAT YOU GET TO DO**

* Leads and drives plant safety culture and puts safety first in all responsibilities.
* Leads identification of opportunities and problem areas for targeted improvement by creating, reviewing and monitoring data or reports that show performance to KPI's. (specifically, safety, quality, waste, and productivity)
* Oversees all aspects of human capital planning & management for the facility, including HC goal setting, improvement targets for KPI's, salary planning, performance management.
* Attract, hire, develop direct reports and create strong succession plans
* Ensure compliance with department safety, product safety, fire protection, Company polices/procedures, and housekeeping programs.
* Ensures effective, timely and well-developed communications for all product associates.
* Manage process control initiatives by ensuring manufacturing SOP's exist, and that they are sufficient for quality, safety, and process control.
* Leads plant budgeting processes
* Ensures execution of plant Cap-Ex
* Lead and ensure growth of CI culture by providing resources, participating in teams, and leading teams as necessary.
* Ensures facility compliance with local, state and federal regulatory agencies.
* Drives employee engagement action planning for the facility
* Leads communication to all plant associates regarding business needs and results
* Leads efforts at Best Practice sharing with other facilities
* Meets safety targets and drives a safety culture and environment to send every employee home everyday without injury.
* Meets or exceeds plant business plan and KPI’s.
* Delivers on established budget.
* Best Practices leadership
* Effective, cost-efficient planning and utilization of manpower, materials and machinery.
* Strong Human Capital planning, development and management for the facility.
* Drives High Performance Culture
* Plant talent to deliver on plan

 **WHAT WE VALUE**
* Strong financial acumen
* Results Orientation / Delivers on Plan
* Team Leadership
* Develops Organizational Capability
* Strategic Orientation / Enterprise Thinker
* Collaboration & Influence
* Change Leadership
* Facility Business Acumen/Market Knowledge

**WHAT WE WANT FROM YOU**

* A Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business administration, or related field
* 10+ years of relevant experience in a production environment
* Demonstrated passion for safety
* 7+ years of leadership experience, preferably in flexible packaging
* Lives Amcor Values and leads by example
* Proven ability to lead and drive continuous improvement
* Strong Customer Service mindset
* Strong written and verbal communication skills
* Demonstrated knowledge of BNA customers and plant capabilities
* Demonstrated understanding of drivers of plant results, including ability to interpret financial results
* Demonstrated CI knowledge, Six Sigma Black Belt certification strongly preferred

**Our Expectations**
====================

We expect our people to be guided by The Amcor Way and demonstrate our Values every day to enable the business to win. We are winning when:

* Our people are engaged and developing as part of a high-performing Amcor team
* Our customers grow and prosper from Amcor’s quality, service, and innovation
* Our investors benefit from Amcor’s consistent growth and superior returns
* The environment is better off because of Amcor’s leadership and products

**Equal Opportunity** **Employer/Minorities/Females/Disabled/Veterans/Sexual** **Orientation/Gender Identity**
==============================================================================================================

Amcor is an Equal Opportunity Employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

If you would like more information about your EEO rights as an applicant under the law, please click on the *"Know Your Rights: Workplace Discrimination is Illegal" Poster*. If, because of a medical condition or disability, you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment process, please call 224-313-7000 and let us know the nature of your request and your contact information.

**E-Verify**
============

We verify the identity and employment authorization of individuals hired for employment in the United States.

**Compensation**
================

The starting salary for this position is expected to be between $176,100 to $242,100 depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Base pay information is based on national averages and a geographic differential may be applied based on work location. Position may also be eligible for Amcor’s Management Incentive Plan / Sales Incentive Plan, which is an annual bonus program based on business and individual performance, as well as medical coverage and other health and welfare benefits. The salary range provided reflects the anticipated starting salary base pay for this role at the time of this posting and does not necessarily reflect full earning potential over the course of employment. This range is applicable to positions performed in jurisdictions with pay transparency requirements, including CA, CO, CT, HI, IL, MD, MA, MN, NV, NJ, NY, RI, VT, WA, Washington DC, as well as remote roles that may be performed in these locations. Compensation for roles performed outside of these jurisdictions may vary. The Company reserves the right to modify this range at any time.

**Benefits**
============

When you join Amcor, you will have access to a comprehensive benefits and compensation package that includes:

* Medical, dental and vision plans
* Flexible time off, starting at 80 hours paid time per year for full-time salaried employees
* Company-paid holidays starting at 8 days per year and may vary by location
* Wellbeing program & Employee Assistance Program
* Health Savings Account/Flexible Spending Account
* Life insurance, AD&D, short-term & long-term disability, and voluntary benefits
* Paid Parental Leave
* Retirement Savings Plan with company match
* Tuition Reimbursement (dependent upon approval)
* Discretionary annual bonus program (initial eligibility dependent upon hire date)

card.title: Plant Manager
card.description:
Job ID: 531039

Exempt

Oldcastle, a CRH company, is reinventing what's possible in building solutions. We are the leading provider of innovative outdoor living products and utility infrastructure solutions for the water, energy, and communications markets throughout North America. We're a trusted and strategic partner to engineers, contractors, distributors, specifiers, retailers, and homeowners alike as the manufacturer of precast concrete, polymer concrete, and plastic infrastructure products. Our portfolio of brands includes Oldcastle APG, Oldcastle Infrastructure, Belgard® hardscape, Echelon® Masonry, RDI® railing, Catalyst™ Fence Solutions, Sakrete® packaged concrete, Amerimix® mortar, Pebble Technology International® pool finishes, and Techniseal® sands and sealant technologies.

Oldcastle Infrastructure - Built For Life from Oldcastle Infrastructure on Vimeo.

**Job Summary**

The Plant Manager is the senior leader on site and is responsible for everything that goes on inside the fence-line and is the driver of the production process. We look to the Plant Manager to build a collaborative environment between operations, sales, engineering, accounting, and transportation. This dynamic leader will be pushing continuous improvement in workplace safety, production efficiency, product cost, and customer service.

**Job Location**

This position will be located at our plant in Sweetwater, TN.

**Job Responsibilities**

 

* Ensure the plant employees and guests on site comply with safety and environmental practices – lead by example and build a safety first culture.
* Lead production scheduling to meet customer needs including timely delivery.
* Develop a keen focus on customer service and proactive communication across the team.
* Partner with the engineering team to ensure proper drawings and designs are being used during the manufacturing process.
* Purchase material/services to successfully operate the facility.
* Successfully hire, supervise, orient, train and retain operations/product staff.
* Promote and maintain a clean workplace that is “tour-ready” at all times.
* Ability to read drawings, plan production tasks from those drawings, and coach employees to produce product correctly.
* Ability to operate some of the standard tools on the plant floor such as overhead cranes, hand tools, batch plant, etc. While the Plant Manager will not be asked to operate these things continuously, having some of these skills will make him/her a better coach and troubleshooter.
* Be a leader and coach leadership. Motivate crews during morning huddles. Lead effective Mid-Day meetings. Coach Leads on how to set expectations on a whiteboard and have them followed. Lead inventory counts. Promote safety best practices in meetings with other Plant Managers.
* Perform any other duties as assigned by the General Manager as deemed appropriate and necessary by them.

**Job Requirements**

 

* Bachelor's Degree in Business, Operations, Engineering or equivalent experience
* 10+ years of experience working in a leadership role in an industrial manufacturing environment
* Experience with precast/concrete or building materials is a plus
* Proven track record of developing, leading and maintaining a continuous improvement mindset at the plant
* Ability to work on your feet for the majority of the day in a production/plant environment subject to areas that are unheated and/or non-air conditioned
* Ability to work with computer as necessary (Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, AX)
* Ability to lead and direct other individuals and work with other group leaders

**What CRH Offers You**

 

* Highly competitive base pay
* Comprehensive medical, dental and disability benefits programs
* Group retirement savings program
* Health and wellness programs
* An inclusive culture that values opportunity for growth, development, and internal promotion

**About CRH**

CRH has a long and proud heritage. We are a collection of hundreds of family businesses, regional companies and large enterprises that together form the CRH family. CRH operates in a decentralized, diversified structure that allows you to work in a small company environment while having the career opportunities of a large international organization.

If you’re up for a rewarding challenge, we invite you to take the first step and apply today! Once you click apply now, you will be brought to our official employment application. Please complete your online profile and it will be sent to the hiring manager. Our system allows you to view and track your status 24 hours a day. Thank you for your interest!

Oldcastle Infrastructure, a CRH Company, is an Affirmative Action and Equal Opportunity Employer.

EOE/Vet/Disability

CRH is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, status as a protected veteran or any other characteristic protected under applicable federal, state, or local law.

AI tools may be used in certain stages of the employment lifecycle, such as candidate review; however, all final employment decisions will be made by a person.

card.title: Director, Hershey Lean System & Manufacturing Transformation
card.description:
Why Hershey:

At The Hershey Company, our culture is rooted in purpose and inspired by Milton Hershey’s enduring vision that business should create opportunity for others. Through our commitment to corporate philanthropy, we create positive impact by supporting communities, helping children thrive, and operating as a business for good. This includes our deep and long standing partnership with Milton Hershey School, where we invest in education, workforce readiness, and hands on engagement to help students succeed beyond the classroom. Supported by strategic grantmaking, product donations, cross brand collaboration, and strong employee volunteerism, Hershey offers a place to work where making a difference—locally and globally—is part of how we do business every day.

 

Location: This role is based in Hershey, PA with an expectation of 3 days in office per week.

**About the Hershey Company**
-----------------------------

At The Hershey Company, we make more moments of goodness through some of the world's most iconic brands, including Hershey's, Reese's, Kit Kat®, Jolly Rancher, Twizzlers, Dot's Pretzels, Lesser Evil and more. Our team supports a global portfolio of over 90 brands, creating opportunities to shape strategies and drive impact across a breadth of businesses that few companies can offer. While many organizations focus on a handful of brands, Hershey provides exposure to a diverse portfolio of category-leading brands enjoyed by consumers around the world. What truly sets us apart is our legacy. Inspired by Milton Hershey's belief that business should create opportunities for others, we have been making a positive impact for more than a century through our commitment to communities, philanthropy, and our longstanding partnership with Milton Hershey School. When you join Hershey, you become part of a company where purpose, growth, and making a difference are woven into how we do business every day.

**How will you fit in the big picture?**
----------------------------------------

The Director, Hershey Lean System & Manufacturing Transformation serves as the enterprise owner of the Hershey Lean Production System, or HLPS, and leads the continued evolution of Lean manufacturing across Hershey’s global manufacturing network.

 

This leader defines strategy, governance, standards, maturity model, deployment approach and capability requirements for HLPS. The Director partners with plant and functional leaders to eliminate systemic losses, strengthen operator ownership and accelerate manufacturing transformation through digital Lean, connected-worker solutions, labor optimization, automation enablement and capacity optimization.

 

The role ensures a consistent enterprise operating system while enabling each site to deploy HLPS according to its business needs, maturity and performance priorities.

**What will you do?**
---------------------

* **Own HLPS strategy and governance:** Define and maintain the HLPS architecture, principles, pillar standards, maturity model, assessment methodology, deployment roadmap and governance routines. Set the multi-year strategy and annual priorities, benchmark externally and translate proven practices into enterprise standards.
* **Lead network deployment:** Partner with Plant Managers to establish site transformation roadmaps, conduct quarterly progress reviews, address enterprise barriers, require recovery plans for material gaps and accelerate the replication of successful practices.
* **Build Lean leadership capability:** Establish role-based capability expectations, learning pathways, qualifications and coaching models for plants, Operational Excellence, engineering and frontline leaders. Build internal coaches and assessors while strengthening Daily Management, Leader Standard Work, structured problem solving, Autonomous Maintenance and Focused Improvement.
* **Advance manufacturing transformation:** Lead strategy and governance for assigned initiatives in digital Lean, connected worker, labor optimization, automation enablement and capacityoptimization. Establish prioritization, pilot criteria, stage gates, value-realization requirements and scalable deployment standards in partnership with Engineering, Supply Chain Strategy, Digital/IT and Finance.
* **Deliver measurable business value:** Translate operational losses and capability gaps into an enterprise improvement portfolio. Connect HLPS maturity to safety, quality, delivery, cost, reliability, productivity and people outcomes, partnering with Finance to validate benefits.
* **Lead and develop the team:** Guide Lean Program Leads and transformation and technical resources, focusing support on the network’s highest-value opportunities.

**Minimum Education & Requirements**
------------------------------------

**Education:**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, operations, supply chain, business or related discipline.
* Master’s degree preferred.

 

**Experience:**

* 10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing, operations, engineering or Operational Excellence, including 5+ years leading leaders, multi-site programs or enterprise-scale manufacturing transformation.
* Demonstrated success designing, deploying or materially advancing Lean, Total Productive Maintenance, or a manufacturing operating system across multiple sites.
* Strong knowledge of Lean management systems, TPM, Daily Management, structured problem solving, loss analysis, asset reliability and capability development.
* Proven ability to influence Plant Managers and senior cross-functional stakeholders without relying on direct authority.
* Strong executive communication, coaching and change-leadership skills.
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or equivalent demonstrated experience preferred.
* Experience in automated or capital-intensive manufacturing is strongly preferred.
* Previous leadership of a manufacturing site, major production operation or enterprise or multi-site Operational Excellence transformation strongly preferred.
* Consumer packaged goods, food and beverage, or other regulated manufacturing experience preferred.

**Benefits and Perks**
----------------------

At Hershey, we offer competitive pay and a comprehensive total rewards package designed to support your wellbeing, financial security, and life outside of work.

* Health & Wellbeing: Medical, dental, and vision coverage, plus wellness programs that support your physical and mental health begin on Day 1.
* Financial Security: Competitive pay, annual incentive opportunities, and a 401(k) with company match
* Time Off & Flexibility: Paid time off, company holidays, and flexible ways of working where applicable
* Growth & Development: Career development programs, learning opportunities, and internal mobility

 

*Benefits may vary based on role, location, and eligibility.*

The anticipated base salary range for this role is $166,400 to $208,000 per year. The actual base salary offered will depend on a variety of job‑related factors, including, but not limited to, experience, skill set, education, and training. In addition to a market-competitive base salary, our Total Rewards package includes performance‑based incentives and a comprehensive, competitive benefits package designed to support overall physical, mental, and financial well‑being (as applicable). Learn more about Hershey’s benefits and all the resources Hershey provides to support our employees’ physical, emotional, and financial well‑being by visiting the Hershey Digital Employee Experience at www.askHRbenefits.hersheys.com

The Hershey Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer. The policy of The Hershey Company is to extend opportunities to qualified applicants and employees on an equal basis regardless of an individual's race, color, gender, age, national origin, religion, citizenship status, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, transgender status, physical or mental disability, protected veteran status, genetic information, pregnancy, or any other categories protected by applicable federal, state or local laws. 
 
The Hershey Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer - Minority/Female/Disabled/Protected Veterans. You may request a reasonable accommodation if you are unable or limited in your ability to use or access our online application process as a result of a disability. 
You can request an accommodation via phone or email.To request an accommodation via phone, please call +1 877-804-1794 and leave a voicemail with your contact information. You may also email a request for accommodation to ApplicationHelp@hersheys.com. Please be sure to include “Accommodation Needed” in the subject line. This will ensure that your email is routed to the appropriate contact who will handle your request.

card.title: Senior Director, Manufacturing, Power Transmission, NA
card.description:
**Date:** Nov 24, 2026

**Location:** Denver, CO, US, 80202

**Company:** Gates Corporation

Are you inspired by challenging the status quo? Do you thrive in collaborative environments that drive results? If so, Gates could be for you.

Gates is a leading manufacturer of application-specific fluid power and power transmission solutions. We push the boundaries of material science to engineer solutions that continually exceed customer expectations.

Let's simplify it, think belts and hoses. Found in motorcycles, conveyor belts, cars, tractors, blenders, vacuum cleaners, bicycles, & 3D printers just to name a few. Because why not do it all?

**Short Description**
---------------------

Gates Corporation has an exciting opportunity for a Sr. Director of Manufacturing, Power Transmission, North America (5 sites). This role will provide leadership and guidance in the development and implementation of product and process improvements for optimal and efficient operation of new and existing products and processes within Gates' North America Power Transmission facilities.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**
-----------------------------------------

* Manage Power Transmission plant operations to deliver daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual operating plan.

card.title: Senior Manager – Industrial Data & Manufacturing Systems Integration
card.description:
Are you looking to power the next leap in the exciting world of advanced electronics?Do you want to help solve problems that drive success in the rapidly evolving technology and connectivity landscape? Then bring your problem-solving, passion, and creativity to help us power the next leap in electronics.
 
 
AtQnity, we’re more than a global leader in materials and solutions for advanced electronics and high-tech industries – we’re a tight-knit team that is motivated by new possibilities, and always up for a challenge. All our dedicated teams contribute to making cutting-edge technology possible. We value forward-thinking challengers, boundary-pushers, and diverse perspectives across all our departments, because we know we play a critical role in the world enabling faster progress for all. Learn how you can start or jumpstart your career with us.
 
 
Senior Manager, Industrial Data& Manufacturing Systems Integration
 
 
**Function:** Integrated Operations& Technology, Digital TechnologyLocation: Wilmington, Delaware, Hybrid (other US Qnity locations may be considered)Travel: Approximately 20–30%Scope: Global, multi-site, and multi-vendor
 
 
Role Summary
 
 
The Senior Manager, Industrial Data& Manufacturing Systems Integration will own the enterprise agenda for industrial data and Level 3 integration across our global manufacturing network.
 
In this role, you will identify, develop, implement, and support two connected sets of systems:
 
 

* The historian and industrial data platform, including EMS/BMS, manufacturing intelligence, advanced analytics and AI, and digital twin capabilities
* The Level 3 integration and middleware layer that supports the platform, including equipment connectivity, edge gateways, orchestration, external-system integration, and twin synchronization

The mandate is to make data contextualization and a standardized edge gateway pattern work at scale. You will bring the architectural judgment needed to make platform decisions and the leadership required to align Manufacturing, Engineering, IT/OT, and external partners. Deep tool expertise will be provided by subject matter experts and specialist hires.
 
 
The Core Challenge
 
 
This role must protect plant-critical data flows and proprietary in-house assets, including custom drivers, tag structures, and site analytics, while establishing sufficient standardization across contextualization models, namespaces, edge patterns, integration contracts, and security.
 
Success requires sound judgment and trusted relationships with plants, engineers, and vendors. The right approach will balance enterprise standards with legitimate local requirements rather than applying a blanket rule such as “everything moves to the cloud” or “nothing leaves the plant.”
 
 
Core Capabilities
 
 
Selection for this role will be based on the following five capabilities, balanced across technical and people leadership. We expect sound architectural judgment, not hands-on expertise in every tool.
 
 
1. Technical Leadership of the Industrial Data and Integration Landscape
 
 
Own the platform decisions, including historian versus lakehouse, integration hub versus custom code, the appropriate edge pattern, and where contextualization should occur.
 
You will frame options; evaluate cost, latency, security, supplier risk, and intellectual property value; engage subject matter experts effectively; and take accountability for the outcome.
 
 
2. Implementing and Supporting Systems in an Operating Plant
 
 
Modernize historians, interfaces, and connectivity that plants rely on continuously without creating data gaps, breaking genealogy, or introducing silent changes to trusted data.
 
You will also establish stable, 24x7 support with clearly defined service levels, controls, and change-management practices.
 
 
3. Stakeholder Engagement and Communication
 
 
Build early sponsorship with Manufacturing, Process Engineering, Quality, Facilities, IT/OT Security, Data& AI, and site leaders across three regions.
 
Explain contextualization, edge technology, and digital twins in terms of business outcomes for audiences ranging from executives to the shop floor. Communicate risks, challenges, and changes early and clearly.
 
 
4. Collaboration Across IT, OT, and External Partners
 
 
Industrial data operates at the intersection of IT and OT and between internal teams and external suppliers.
 
Maintain OT-grade standards for segmentation, edge design, and change control while building effective partnerships with Controls, OT Security, subject matter experts, system integrators, and vendors.
 
 
5. Followership and Change Leadership Across Sites
 
 
Our Wilmington, Cheonan, and Hsinchu sites differ in regulatory requirements, engineering culture, and language. Common standards may encounter legitimate local concerns.
 
Build strong teams, determine what must be standardized and what may remain local, bring sites through the change, and stand behind both decisions.
 
 
Key Responsibilities
 
 
Vision, Strategy, and Architecture
 
 

* Establish the multi-year strategy, roadmap, and ISA-95-aligned reference architecture for the industrial data platform and Level 3 integration layer.
* Govern a fit-for-purpose framework that determines what belongs in the historian, cloud platform, edge environment, integration hub, or custom code.
* Establish data contextualization as an enterprise capability by owning the common asset model, Unified Namespace, and contextualization standards across equipment, process, quality, energy, and facilities data.
* Standardize a secure, outbound-only edge gateway pattern for connectivity, protocol translation, buffering, and edge processing, enabling new equipment and sites to connect efficiently.

Historian and Data Platform Ownership
 
 

* Identify, implement, and support enterprise historians, such as AspenTech InfoPlus.21, including tag governance, retention, high availability, and migration.
* Develop and operate cloud data platforms, including Microsoft Fabric and Databricks, for time-series, contextualized, and EMS/BMS data, with governed data products and access controls.
* Deliver manufacturing intelligence, AI, and digital twin capabilities using platforms such as Seeq, Siemens Insights Hub, Cognite Data Fusion, and Azure Digital Twins.
* Establish the industrial knowledge model and appropriate responsible-AI controls.

Level 3 Integration, Edge, and Middleware Ownership
 
 

* Deploy and support equipment connectivity and edge gateways using technologies such as PTC Kepware, Litmus Edge, Ignition, and Azure IoT Operations across OPC UA, MQTT, SECS/GEM, and Modbus.
* Build and operate the Unified Namespace and contextualization layer using technologies such as HighByte Intelligence Hub, HiveMQ, and MQTT/Sparkplug B.
* Own orchestration and external-system integration using platforms such as Boomi and MuleSoft across MES, historians, digital twins, ERP, PLM, QMS, LIMS, and WMS, including twin synchronization.
* Ensure OT cybersecurity, data governance, and 24x7 resilience for data flows that are critical to shop-floor operations.
* Apply relevant standards and architectural models, including IEC 62443 and Purdue/DMZ principles.

Delivery and Support
 
 

* Own the complete system lifecycle, from business case development through design, implementation, hypercare, and ongoing support.
* Establish service levels, CI/CD practices, and OT-grade change control.
* Manage scope, budget, risk, and benefits across concurrent global rollouts.
* Coordinate platform suppliers, system integrators, and managed-service partners.

Leadership, Stakeholder Engagement, and Team Development
 
 

* Partner with Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, Facilities, IT/OT Security, MES, and Data& AI.
* Communicate technology strategy, business value, risks, and progress to executive stakeholders.
* Lead change management and adoption at each site.
* Build and develop a global team of architects, engineers, and product owners.
* Add subject matter experts and specialist capabilities where deeper technical expertise is required.

Required Qualifications
 
 
These qualifications represent minimum thresholds and are not the sole basis for selection.
 
 

* 8 or more years of experience in manufacturing IT/OT, including the delivery and support of historian, industrial data, MES, or OT integration systems in semiconductor, electronics, or similarly complex manufacturing environments.
* Five or more years of experience leading distributed teams and multi-vendor programs with accountability for budgets and business benefits.
* Strong command of ISA-95, the Purdue model, contextualization and asset modeling, edge gateway architecture, OPC UA, MQTT, and OT security, with the ability to set direction and effectively challenge technical experts.
* Demonstrated stakeholder engagement and communication skills across audiences ranging from executives to the shop floor.
* A record of building teams and leading change across multiple sites.
* Commercial experience with RFx processes, contracts, licensing, and vendor governance.
* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, computer science, or a related field.

Preferred Qualifications
 
 
The following qualifications may strengthen an application but do not replace the core capabilities and are not intended as initial screening requirements.
 
 

* Experience delivering at least one historian, data-platform, or integration modernization within an operating plant without loss of data continuity.
* Experience taking at least one greenfield or significant new-site deployment through implementation and into stable support.
* Experience in semiconductor manufacturing, advanced packaging, or specialty materials.
* Working proficiency in Korean or Mandarin.
* Experience with technologies such as AVEVA PI, Seeq, Cognite Data Fusion, HighByte Intelligence Hub, PTC Kepware, or Databricks.
* Experience delivering an enterprise-scale Unified Namespace, digital twin, or manufacturing AI capability.
* Relevant certifications such as PMP, SAFe, TOGAF, ISA/IEC 62443, Microsoft Azure, or Databricks.
* Experience in regulated-quality environments, including ISO 9001, IATF 16949, or GxP.
* Master’s degree or MBA.

Technical Environment
 
 
You will identify, develop, implement, and support the systems below while reshaping the technology landscape over time.
 
Many sites currently rely on in-house tools and point-to-point connections. You will determine what should be standardized, rationalized, migrated, or retained where it provides proprietary value. You are expected to understand how the components fit together and make sound platform decisions. Specialist depth will be provided by subject matter experts.
 
 
Historian and Data Platforms
 
 
**Technologies you may encounter or help select:** 

* Wonderware
* AspenTech InfoPlus.21
* Microsoft Fabric
* Databricks

Manufacturing Intelligence and AI
 
 
Technologies and capabilities you may encounter or help select:
 
 

* Seeq
* Siemens Insights Hub
* Azure AI and Copilot
* EMS/BMS energy and facilities data

Digital Twin and Knowledge Model
 
 
**Technologies and approaches you may encounter or help select:** 

* Cognite Data Fusion
* Azure Digital Twins
* ISA-95 asset hierarchies
* Industrial knowledge graphs

Edge Gateways and Equipment Connectivity
 
 
**Technologies and protocols you may encounter or help select:** 

* PTC Kepware
* Litmus Edge
* Ignition
* Azure IoT Operations
* OPC UA
* SECS/GEM
* Modbus
* PLC, DCS, and SCADA environments

Data Contextualization and DataOps
 
 
**Technologies and approaches you may encounter or help select:** 

* HighByte Intelligence Hub
* HiveMQ
* MQTT/Sparkplug B
* Unified Namespace
* ISA-95 asset models

Enterprise Integration
 
 
**Technologies and systems you may encounter or help select:** 

* Boomi
* MuleSoft
* MES
* SAP
* PLM
* QMS
* LIMS
* WMS

Standards and Security
 
 
**Standards and frameworks you may apply:** 

* ISA-95
* Purdue model
* IEC 62443
* NIST Cybersecurity Framework
* OPC UA companion specifications
* SEMI E30 and E164

Living the Qnity Values
 
 
At Qnity, success is measured not only bywhat we achieve, but also byhow we achieve it.
 
 

* Customer: Partner with stakeholders to understand needs, solve business challenges, and deliver meaningful outcomes.
* Innovation: Continuously improve processes, technologies, and ways of working.
* Speed: Act with urgency, focus, and precision to move work forward and deliver results.
* People: Build trusted relationships, collaborate across teams, and inspire positive change.

Join ourTalent Community to stay connected with us!
 
 
Qnity is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, national origin, age, veteran status, disability or any other protected class. If you need a reasonable accommodation to search or apply for a position, please visit our Accessibility Page for Contact Information.
 
 
Qnity offers a comprehensive pay and benefits package. To learn more visit theCompensation and Benefits page.
 
 
We use Artificial Intelligence (AI) to enhance our recruitment process.
 
The Pay range for this role is $108,500.00 - $170,500.00 Annual
 
**How Base Pay is Determined:** Qnity has job leveling frameworks that help organize roles based on progressive levels of responsibility, proficiency and qualifications. Each role has an associated pay range (or an established pay rate for some roles) based on the competitive market in each country where we operate. Each individual’s pay is based on a variety of factors, including their role and the associated pay range for that role, their geographic location (i.e., country, state, metropolitan area), as well as their skills, experience, education and certifications, and performance.

card.description:
**Be visionary**

Teledyne Technologies Incorporated provides enabling technologies for industrial growth markets that require advanced technology and high reliability. These markets include aerospace and defense, factory automation, air and water quality environmental monitoring, electronics design and development, oceanographic research, deepwater oil and gas exploration and production, medical imaging and pharmaceutical research.

We are looking for individuals who thrive on making an impact and want the excitement of being on a team that wins.

**Job Description**

The Director, Inventory Management & Operational Excellence will lead a new enterprise team that brings inventory back to plan and keeps it there. The role installs a standard inventory management system at Teledyne sites: control of the material coming in, sound stocking policy and planning, and regular reviews that turn data into decisions. The Director leads the program and works hands-on at one site at a time, starting in our defense businesses.

A key part of this role involves partnering with Segment leadership, site General Managers, Operations, Supply Chain, and Finance teams to set standard work, build site capability, and deliver sustainable business results, supporting enterprise objectives for working capital, on-time delivery, and margin.

**This role requires up to 75% travel. Due to the extensive travel involved, candidates may be based anywhere within the United States.**

**Job Duties and Responsibilities**

* Lead standard site assessments of planning maturity, part-level inventory, and forecast accuracy, and partner with site leadership to prioritize and execute improvement opportunities.
* Set and deploy baseline standard work for every site, including weekly action on MRP messages for open purchase orders, receiving to plan, monthly inventory forecast reporting, and documented decisions on excess, obsolete, and aged WIP inventory.
* Drive inventory optimization and working capital improvement initiatives across the organization. Lead tactical controls on open purchase orders and receipts first, then structural fixes to safety stock, min/max settings, inventory entitlement, and planning.
* Own the guiding metric: material and labor going into inventory vs. cost of goods shipped, tracked monthly and forecast a year ahead, so sites act before inventory builds.
* Establish and implement enterprise inventory policies, standards, and governance, including decision rights for buying ahead of demand, keeping excess, and disposing of obsolete material.
* Run the monthly enterprise inventory review with senior leadership, using KPI dashboards to monitor every site, identify gaps, and drive accountability.
* Co-lead each site’s weekly material exception review and monthly General Manager inventory review, then coach site leaders to run them on their own.
* Strengthen SIOP, demand forecasting, and make-to-stock or make-to-order decisions with site planning teams, from opportunity identification through implementation and sustainment.
* Leverage AI-enabled technologies, automation, and advanced analytics to improve inventory decisions, reporting, and business performance.
* Capture what works at each site in a standard playbook and share best practices across the enterprise.
* Lead and develop a team of one Manager and two Inventory Analysts working two sites at a time.

**Education and Experience**

* Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Business, or related field.
* MBA preferred.
* 10+ years of leadership experience in Operations, Supply Chain, Materials Management, or Operational Excellence, including site-level operations or supply chain leadership.
* APICS CPIM or CSCP, or Lean Six Sigma Black Belt, preferred.
* Experience supporting multi-site manufacturing and global business environments.
* Ability to travel up to 75%, including extended on-site periods during site engagements, to work with site teams, run operational reviews, and develop site leaders across Teledyne business units.

**Qualifications and Competencies**

* Proven ability to lead cross-functional improvement initiatives and deliver measurable inventory and working capital results.
* Deep knowledge of materials management and supply chain planning, including MRP, open purchase order management, safety stock and inventory policy, SIOP, and demand forecasting.
* Working knowledge of Lean, Standard Work, and Root Cause Problem Solving.
* Experience deploying and sustaining business systems or enterprise operating models across multiple sites or business units, with hands-on factory and supply chain experience.
* Strong analytical, problem-solving, and project management skills.
* Passion for continuous improvement, emerging technologies, AI-enabled business transformation, and operational excellence.

* Excellent communication, coaching, and leadership skills, including leading site teams without direct authority.
* Experience utilizing KPI dashboards, operational scorecards, and performance management systems.
* Experience working in ERP systems (SAP preferred) and across multiple ERP environments.

**Due to the type of work performed and facility access requirements, applicants must be a "U.S. Person" (U.S. Citizen, U.S. National, lawful permanent resident, asylee, or refugee).**

**This role requires up to 75% travel. Due to the extensive travel involved, candidates may be based anywhere within the United States.**

card.title: Director, Advanced Manufacturing Engineering
card.description:
**At a Glance**

**Legrand** has an exciting opportunity for a **Director of Advanced Manufacturing Engineering** to join the **Electrical Infrastructure division.** This leader identifies, develops, industrializes, and scales manufacturing processes, automation, autonomation, equipment, and digital capabilities that improve safety, quality, service, productivity, capacity, and flexibility across the manufacturing network.

The Director of Advanced Manufacturing Engineering advises, develops, and executes operational business strategies with the VP of Operations and EI division Leadership Team in support of EI growth and financial goals. Those strategies include footprint and capacity expansion, factory roles, insourcing/outsourcing, operating constraints, and growth enablement into a multiyear manufacturing technology roadmap. The role provides technical leadership for significant manufacturing investments, establishes common engineering and equipment standards, and ensures solutions are economically justified, successfully industrialized, and deliver sustained operating and financial results.

The Director of Advanced Manufacturing Engineering is expected to determine when advanced technology creates differentiated value and when a simpler process, equipment, maintenance, sourcing, or product solution is more appropriate.

This position leads a focused technical organization that works through plant resources, internal partners, equipment suppliers, and qualified integrators.

**What Will You Do?**

**Manufacturing Technology Strategy**

* Develop and maintain a multiyear advanced manufacturing roadmap aligned with business strategy, factory roles, product requirements, capacity needs, and footprint plans.
* Evaluate and deploy appropriate manufacturing technologies, including automation, autonomation, robotics, machine vision, controls, advanced tooling, and digital manufacturing systems.
* Identify manufacturing capabilities the division should protect, build, standardize, modernize, source externally, or retire.
* Adapt technology strategies to differences in product complexity, volume, mix, demand stability, and operating model.

**Opportunity Portfolio and Investment Leadership**

* Build and prioritize a network-wide portfolio of advanced manufacturing, automation, and equipment-modernization opportunities.
* Define the operating loss or constraint being addressed, credible alternatives, expected business impact, investment requirement, lifecycle cost, risk, payback, and sustainment requirements.
* Determine when technology creates differentiated value and when process redesign, tooling, equipment refurbishment, maintenance improvement, outsourcing, product redesign, or another solution is more appropriate.
* Serve as the division’s technical authority for significant manufacturing technology and equipment investments.
* Support footprint, make-versus-buy, capacity, and capital-allocation decisions with clear technical facts and alternatives.
* Lead the division governance process for manufacturing capital planning and deployment, providing consolidated visibility to investment requirements, approvals, timing, expenditure, implementation risk, and expected benefits.
* Partner with Operations, business General Managers, and Finance to develop and maintain a prioritized multi-year manufacturing plan.
* Monitor the deployment of approved manufacturing investments and escalate material risks involving scope, cost, schedule, technical performance, plant readiness, or benefit realization.

**Technical Industrialization and Standards**

* Establish standards for manufacturing equipment, automation, controls, tooling, data connectivity, safety, maintainability, and industrialization.
* Lead technical reviews of equipment specifications, process concepts, integrator selection, designs, risk assessments, acceptance testing, process capability, documentation, training, and critical spares.
* Ensure new processes incorporate quality at source, error-proofing, equipment reliability, operator safety, cybersecurity, and appropriate performance visibility.
* Establish preferred technology platforms, reusable equipment concepts, and qualified supplier and integrator networks where standardization creates value.

**Deployment and Sustainable Results**

* Lead the technical delivery of selected high-value, high-risk, or highly replicable manufacturing initiatives.
* Define when central AME involvement is required and when plant teams can execute within established standards.
* Establish clear ownership for technical development, plant readiness, commissioning, production ramp, and ongoing sustainment.
* Transfer solutions to plant ownership after safety, capability, reliability, training, documentation, maintenance, and performance requirements have been met.
* Conduct post-implementation reviews to verify that operating and financial benefits are achieved and sustained.
* Capture lessons learned and creates replication methods for proven solutions.

**Organization and Capability Development**

* Build and develop a high-performance advanced manufacturing engineering team with the technical depth required to support the division’s strategy.
* Define which capabilities should be retained internally and which should be accessed through plants, internal partners, equipment suppliers, engineering firms, or system integrators.
* Establish expectations for supplier and integrator performance, documentation, intellectual property, lifecycle support, and reuse of developed solutions.
* Develop plant technical capability to minimize long-term dependence on central resources or external partners.

**Education:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Automation Engineering, or a related technical field.

**Experience:**

* At least 10 years of progressive experience in advanced manufacturing engineering, automation, process engineering, or industrialization, including five years leading technical teams or multisite programs.
* Demonstrated experience in automation, robotics, autonomation, controls, machine vision, advanced tooling, or manufacturing data systems.
* Experience with equipment specifications, integrator management, design reviews, acceptance testing, commissioning, capability validation, and production handoff.
* Broad manufacturing-process knowledge and experience in both high-mix and higher-volume environments.
* Proven record of turning manufacturing technology investments into sustained operating and financial results.

**Skills/Knowledge/Abilities:**

* Strong understanding of capital economics, lifecycle cost, capacity analysis, labor impact, and benefit realization.
* Ability to translate operating losses and business requirements into prioritized technical opportunities.
* Ability to determine when advanced technology is appropriate and when a simpler operational solution will create greater value.
* Ability to translate technical complexity into clear business decisions and influence across a matrixed organization.
* Strong cross-functional collaboration with Operations, Finance, Product Engineering, Quality, EHS, HR, IT, Supply Chain, Lean, and PMO teams.
* Strong supplier, equipment manufacturer, and system-integrator management capabilities.
* Ability to balance enterprise standardization with legitimate differences across products, processes, plants, and operating models.
* Demonstrated ability to lead technical professionals, develop organizational capability, and operate effectively across multiple businesses and manufacturing locations.

Legrand is the global specialist in electrical and digital building infrastructures. Its comprehensive offering of solutions for residential, commercial, and datacenter markets makes it a benchmark for customers worldwide.

Bridging power from sources to pathways to touchpoints, Legrand’s Electrical Infrastructure division combines innovation and quality to provide leading solutions for an evolving energy landscape. Our expertly designed products enable customers to confidently address the complex needs and challenges of electrification, while enhancing everyday experiences like plugging in, switching on, and staying connected. Committed to best-in-class service at every stage, we act as a trusted partner for our customers to ensure each project’s success and their continued satisfaction. Legrand's Electrical Infrastructure division includes the following brands and product lines: Girtz, Avtron, Power Bus Way, Cablofil, Connectrac, Wiremold and Pass & Seymour.

Legrand, North & Central America offers comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, as well as distinctive benefits like a high employer 401K match, paid time off (PTO) and holiday pay, short-term and long-term disability benefit plans, above-benchmark paid maternity and parental leave, bonus opportunities in accordance with the Company’s incentive plans, paid time off to volunteer, and an active/growing Employee Resource Group network. For more information, visit legrand.us.

card.title: Plant Manager
card.description:
**Job Summary**

The position of **Plant Manager** is responsible for directing, coordinating, and managing the overall facility operation in conjunction with the customer’s production requirements. Ensure facility production objectives are achieved at the lowest cost consistent with IATF16949 quality requirements. Delegate production leadership responsibilities to achieve the desired objectives set forth in the corporate business plan while maintaining compliance to Federal, State, and Local Safety and Environmental regulations and laws.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Plant Operation
 + Coordinate with the operations manager in the execution of production schedules based on sales requirements and plant capacity.
 + Coordinate and communicate with leadership team and department managers in meeting production goals while focusing on continuous improvement and cost reduction initiatives.
 + Schedule manufacturing activities based on customer releases to minimize inventory.
 + Ensure orders are released in chronological order (FIFO) unless circumstances dictate a change in customer needs.
 + Ensure all “work in process” is properly tagged in accordance with procedures and instructions.
 + Receive and review daily shift reports from leadership team and address areas of concern.
* Ensure the production floor is well equipped, well maintained and efficiently designed
 + Per the IATF16949 requirements, ensure that production floor is equipped with proper work instructions and procedures to carry out production activities.
 + Ensure properly maintained equipment and appropriate trained personnel are available to carry out these activities.
 + Work with operations, program management, and process engineering teams to ensure new programs and process changes are implemented within designated launch plan requirements.
 + Support new program launches and engineer changes that may include floor layouts, staffing, quality and/or tooling requirements.
 + Provide continuous review of departmental processes to improve overall efficiencies.
 + Ensure facility management, making sure the facility meets all production operation requirements.
* Adherence to established policies, processes and procedures
 + Work with leadership team to enforce written policies and procedures to ensure consistency and fairness while maintaining a healthy and safe work environment.
 + Review and approve recommendations of subordinates in matters of position changes and promotions.
 + Work with leadership team to identify and record any issues relating to process failures, policy or procedure violations, or quality system failures
 + When and where required, assist leadership team with attendance management, performance management and corrective action of employees.
* Assist with implementation and compliance of all health, safety, environmental and quality control plans
 + Work with quality department to ensure adherence to the IATF16949 quality standards and corporate quality best practices.
 + Review and disposition of nonconforming products.
 + Assist in providing solutions to prevent reoccurrence.
 + Ensure consistency with implementation and adherence of the company health, safety and environmental policies and processes.
 + Ensure compliance with Federal, State and Local regulatory requirements such as OSHA, EPA, etc.
 + Be visible, assume leadership, and assist in developing and initiating an effective health and safety attitude. Participate and initiate in continuous safety training.

**Qualifications**

* Education
 + Minimum Required: Associates Degree or Technical Accreditation
 + Preferred: Bachelor’s Degree in Business Management, Administration or equivalent
* Experience
 + Minimum Required: 5+ years working in a production environment
 + 2+ years working in a manager or supervisory role in manufacturing/production environment
 + Preferred: 5+ years working in a managerial role in a manufacturing/production environment
* Must have and maintain a valid Driver’s License
* Strong technical background and a general understanding of a manufacturing/production process
* Fluent in English (verbal, reading, writing)
* Must be team-oriented and have excellent communication, organizational and computer literacy skills
* Requires a high level of professionalism and strong work ethic
* Preferred: Familiarity with TS16949 or IATF 16949, Quality Audits, and Environmental Management System and OSHA Requirements

**Working Conditions**

The following working conditions are present or expected on a daily basis:

* Manufacturing/production floor environment with a presence on the production floor required for at least 50% of daily work time.
* Frequent exposure to industrial manufacturing, automotive vehicles, weather elements, chemicals and robotics.
* Personal protective equipment must be worn at all times on the production floor.

**IMPORTANT NOTE**

The organization reserves the right to change, amend or disuse this job description at any time. This document is intended to provide an overview of the required responsibilities and qualifications.

**WHO WE ARE**

As the largest private-sector power producer in the world and the nation's largest producer of clean and reliable energy, Constellation is focused on our purpose: lighting the way to a brilliant tomorrow for all. We have been the leader in clean energy production for more than a decade, and we are cultivating a workplace where our employees can grow, thrive, and contribute. Now integrated with Calpine, our portfolio includes 55 gigawatts of capacity from nuclear, natural gas, geothermal, hydro, wind and solar facilities, with the generating capacity to power the equivalent of 27 million homes. 
 
Our culture and employee experience make it clear: We are powered by passion and purpose. Together, we're creating healthier communities and a cleaner planet, and our people are the driving force behind our success. At Constellation, you can build a fulfilling career with opportunities to learn, grow and make an impact. By doing our best work and meeting new challenges, we can accomplish great things. Join us in meeting the country's energy needs today and tomorrow.

**TOTAL REWARDS**

Constellation offers an extensive selection of benefits and rewards to help our employees thrive professionally and personally. We provide competitive compensation and a wide-range of benefits that support both employees and their families, helping them prepare for the future. In addition to highly competitive salaries, eligible employees are offered a bonus program, 401(k) with company match, employee stock purchase program; comprehensive medical, dental and vision benefits, including robust wellbeing programs; disability and life insurance benefits; paid time off for vacation, holidays, and sick days; and much more.

Expected salary range of $189,000 to $210,000, varies based on experience, along with comprehensive benefits package that includes bonus and 401(k).

Responsibilities:

**PRIMARY PURPOSE OF POSITION**

Manage and oversee the safe, efficient and reliable operation of fossil or hydro station(s). Ensure compliance with all federal, state and local regulatory requirements, applicable industry technical standards and company policies. Operate the plant(s) in a manner that minimizes the cost of generation and maximizes profitability while maintaining the long-term viability of the station assets.

 

**PRIMARY DUTIES AND ACCOUNTABILITIES**

* Ensure standards are established and implemented to provide a safe work environment.
* Effectively manage all resources to ensure generation of electricity in a timely and reliable manner at the direction of the Power Team.
* Maintain a positive work environment and good employee relations. Provide guidance for employee development opportunities and timely feedback regarding performance.
* Serve as a change agent for business initiatives, while assuring the human element is understood and considered
* Manage the station O&M and capital budgets to minimize costs and maximize profitability while ensuring the long-term viability of the assets.
* Ensure compliance with all federal, state and local regulatory requirements and maintain environmental stewardship.
* Maintain effective community relations to promote a positive image of the Company.
* Perform all other duties as assigned.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

* BS in engineering or business
* Minimum of 10 years professional experience
* Minimum of 8 years power plant (or related) experience
* Minimum of 5 years supervisory/managerial experience
* Professional or technical level experience in a technical role at a power plant
* Operations
* At least 2 of the following: Corporate/Staff, Engineering, Maintenance, or Outage
* RHR Selection

Qualifications:

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Master's Degree in engineering, business or related field
* Multi-site experience
* Multi-departmental experience
* Collective bargaining experience

Now integrated with Calpine, our portfolio includes 55 gigawatts of capacity from nuclear, natural gas, geothermal, hydro, wind and solar facilities, with the generating capacity to power the equivalent of 27 million homes. 
 
Our culture and employee experience make it clear: We are powered by passion and purpose. Together, we're creating healthier communities and a cleaner planet, and our people are the driving force behind our success. At Constellation, you can build a fulfilling career with opportunities to learn, grow and make an impact. By doing our best work and meeting new challenges, we can accomplish great things. Join us in meeting the country's energy needs today and tomorrow.

**TOTAL REWARDS**

Constellation offers an extensive selection of benefits and rewards to help our employees thrive professionally and personally. We provide competitive compensation and a wide-range of benefits that support both employees and their families, helping them prepare for the future. In addition to highly competitive salaries, eligible employees are offered a bonus program, 401(k) with company match, employee stock purchase program; comprehensive medical, dental and vision benefits, including robust wellbeing programs; disability and life insurance benefits; paid time off for vacation, holidays, and sick days; and much more.

Expected salary range of $189,000 to $210,000, varies based on experience, along with comprehensive benefits package that includes bonus and 401(k).

Responsibilities:

**PRIMARY PURPOSE OF POSITION**

Manage and oversee the safe, efficient and reliable operation of fossil or hydro station(s). Ensure compliance with all federal, state and local regulatory requirements, applicable industry technical standards and company policies. Operate the plant(s) in a manner that minimizes the cost of generation and maximizes profitability while maintaining the long-term viability of the station assets.

 

**PRIMARY DUTIES AND ACCOUNTABILITIES**

* Ensure standards are established and implemented to provide a safe work environment.
* Effectively manage all resources to ensure generation of electricity in a timely and reliable manner at the direction of the Power Team.
* Maintain a positive work environment and good employee relations. Provide guidance for employee development opportunities and timely feedback regarding performance.

card.title: Senior Manager, Project Management - External Manufacturing
card.description:
Rezolute is a pre-commercial ultra-rare disease company focused on significantly improving outcomes for individuals with hypoglycemia caused by hyperinsulinism (HI). Our fully human monoclonal antibody therapy, RZ358 (ersodetug), is designed to treat all forms of HI and has shown substantial benefit in clinical trials and real-world use for the treatment of congenital hyperinsulinism (cHI) and tumor hyperinsulinism (tHI).

**Position Summary**

Rezolute is seeking a proactive, execution-focused project management professional to coordinate external manufacturing programs as the company advances toward commercial manufacturing.

The Senior Manager, Project Management - External Manufacturing will manage integrated plans, communications, and deliverables across technology transfer, GMP manufacturing, process characterization, process validation, and commercial readiness. Working with internal functional leads and contract development and manufacturing organizations (CDMOs), this individual will align schedules, supplier commitments, and cross-functional dependencies with Rezolute’s Plan of Record (POR), supply requirements, and business priorities.

This role owns project coordination and follow-through, not technical oversight. External Manufacturing Operations, Manufacturing Science and Technology (MSAT), Quality Assurance (QA), and designated functional experts retain responsibility for technical strategy, scientific assessments, manufacturing process decisions, and quality approvals.

### **Principal Duties and Responsibilities**

Integrated Project Planning and Execution

* Develop and maintain integrated project plans for external Drug Substance (DS) and Drug Product (DP) programs, defining scope, deliverables, owners, milestones, dependencies, and target dates.

* Align project baselines and supplier commitments with the POR, supply requirements, and approved priorities.

* Monitor critical-path activities and progress against plan; coordinate recovery actions for overdue or at-risk commitments with functional owners and suppliers.

* Assess scope, schedule, and resource changes with accountable stakeholders and route proposed changes through established approval processes.

Communications and Cross-Functional Coordination

* Serve as the project management point of contact between Rezolute teams and CDMOs, facilitating cross-functional coordination and timely communication of changes.

* Lead internal and supplier project meetings, using focused agendas to address progress, upcoming deliverables, dependencies, and decisions required.

* Maintain and distribute meeting records and action items with clear owners and due dates; drive follow-through to closure.

Workstream and Milestone Coordination

* Coordinate manufacturing and milestone readiness by tracking prerequisites, including material availability, documentation, internal reviews, and supplier deliverables.

* Integrate technical and quality review timelines into project schedules, including protocols, reports, and master or electronic batch records.

* Track schedule dependencies associated with change controls, deviations, investigations, and other quality-system activities in partnership with QA and technical owners.

* Coordinate handoffs from development and validation activities to routine commercial manufacturing, tracking agreed deliverables, receiving owners, and outstanding actions.

Risk, Issue, and Decision Management

* Maintain risk, issue, assumption, decision, and dependency logs, including accountable owners and required completion dates.

* Work with functional leads and suppliers to assess execution risks and track mitigation actions and residual risks.

* Facilitate issue resolution and escalate unresolved items or pending decisions, clearly communicating timing requirements and potential project impacts.

Reporting, Scope, and Project Controls

* Provide dashboards and leadership updates showing milestone performance, forecast completion dates, critical-path activities, risks, and decisions or intervention required.

* Partner with External Manufacturing leadership, Supplier Relationship Management (SRM), Business, and Procurement to define milestones, deliverables, assumptions, and timelines in supplier scopes of work.

* Support project-level financial tracking with budget owners, including planned work, supplier milestones, and the budget and schedule impacts of scope changes.

* Improve project management tools, reporting practices, and lessons-learned processes across the external manufacturing network.

### **Qualifications/Requirements:**

* Bachelor’s degree in a scientific, engineering, business, project management, or related discipline.

* Minimum of seven years of relevant biopharmaceutical industry experience, including responsibility for managing cross-functional projects involving CDMOs or other external manufacturing partners.

* Demonstrated ability to manage integrated schedules, critical-path activities, risks, and changing priorities across multiple workstreams.

* Experience coordinating technology transfer, GMP manufacturing, process characterization, process validation, or commercial manufacturing readiness activities.

* Working knowledge of biopharmaceutical manufacturing and cGMP requirements sufficient to understand project dependencies and engage effectively with technical and quality teams.

* Strong meeting facilitation, written communication, and stakeholder management skills, including communication with external partners and senior leadership.

* Ability to translate technical discussions into clear project actions, decisions, and schedule implications while respecting functional decision-making authority.

* Strong organization, attention to detail, and follow-through, with the ability to drive accountability and prioritize independently in a matrixed environment.

* Proficiency in Smartsheet or comparable project management software and Microsoft Teams, Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.

Preferred Qualifications:

* Experience supporting late-stage biologics programs transitioning to commercial manufacturing.

* Experience coordinating DS and/or DP manufacturing projects across multiple external partners.

* Experience working in a small to mid-sized biotechnology company.

* Experience tracking project budgets, supplier scopes of work, and change requests.

Core Competencies:

* Project Planning and Controls: Creates practical plans that connect workstreams and support timely delivery.

* Execution and Accountability: Establishes ownership and follows through on commitments.

* Communication and Collaboration: Builds productive relationships and keeps internal and external teams aligned.

* Risk and Issue Management: Anticipates challenges, coordinates mitigation, and escalates appropriately.

* Adaptability and Prioritization: Adjusts plans as circumstances change while maintaining focus on program objectives.

Rezolute (RZLT) currently anticipates the base salary for Senior Manager - Project Management External Manufacturing role could range from $165,000 to $180,000 and will depend, in part, on the successful candidate’s geographical location and their qualifications for the role, including education and experience. This position will also be eligible for an annual performance bonus in accordance with the terms of the applicable plan (depending, in part, on company and individual performance and at the Company’s discretion on an individual basis). The compensation described above is subject to change and could be higher or lower than the range described based on current market survey data and the qualifications, education, experience and geographical location of the selected candidate.

Qualifying employees are eligible to participate in benefit programs such as:

* Health Insurance (Medical / Dental / Vision)

* Disability, Life & Long-Term Care Insurance

* Holiday Pay

* Tracking Free Vacation Program

* 401(k) Plan Match

* Educational Assistance Benefit

* Fitness Center Reimbursement

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and do not discriminate against applicants due to race, ethnicity, gender, veteran status, or on the basis of disability or any other federal, state or local protected class.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.
