card.title: Director, HR – U.S. Commercial & Manufacturing
card.description:
Vantive is a vital organ therapy company on a mission to extend lives and expand possibilities for patients and care teams everywhere. For 70 years, our team has driven meaningful innovations in kidney care. As we build on our legacy, we are deepening our commitment to elevating the dialysis experience through digital solutions and advanced services, while looking beyond kidney care and investing in transforming vital organ therapies. Greater flexibility and efficiency in therapy administration for care teams, and longer, fuller lives for patients— that is what Vantive aspires to deliver.

We believe Vantive will not only build our leadership in the kidney care space, it will also offer meaningful work to those who join us. At Vantive, you will become part of a community of people who are focused, courageous and don’t settle for the mediocre. Each of us is driven to help improve patients’ lives worldwide. Join us in advancing our mission to extend lives and expand possibilities.

This position serves as the senior strategic people leader and trusted advisor to the SVP – U.S. General Manager and the U.S. Executive Leadership Team, overseeing HR for U.S. Field Sales, U.S. Marketing, and U.S. Manufacturing (approximately 950 employees). The leader shapes and executes the HR strategy that enables business objectives and builds the organizational capability and culture required for sustained growth.

**Critical Responsibilities**

* Lead, develop, and inspire the HR team supporting these organizations, setting priorities, performance expectations, and a high-performing culture
* Sit on the U.S. Commercial Leadership Team and the Americas HR Leadership Team, building influential cross-functional partnerships
* Design and deliver business-specific HR solutions that measurably advance business outcomes
* Provide executive-level counsel to senior leaders, managers, and employees
* Provide thought leadership and accountability for culture, integration, organizational design, leadership development, and large-scale change management
* Apply strong analytical skills, strategic judgment, and financial acumen, including knowledge of the organization’s financial position, long-range plans, culture, and competitive landscape, to shape decisions and influence senior stakeholders
* Assess the effectiveness of the organization’s business model and dynamics, and lead realignment as needed to drive performance
* Lead strategic workforce planning and advise senior leadership on hiring, headcount, and organizational design decisions
* Advise site leaders and the HR team on manufacturing employee relations, engagement, and compliance, driving consistent HR practices across U.S. sites

**Risk, Governance & Compliance**

* Bring demonstrable experience in employee relations, labor relations, and compliance, and develop and manage the labor relations strategy
* Advise on organizational change related to automation, restructuring, new product launches, digital transformation, and expansion
* Partner with Legal to mitigate people-related risks and ensure alignment with local regulations and corporate standards

**Key Qualifications**

* Exceptional experience partnering with senior leaders, people managers, and employees in a highly matrixed, multi-site global environment
* Deep expertise across HR disciplines, including integration and transformation, talent acquisition, performance management, compensation, culture and engagement, change management, organizational design, and inclusion & diversity
* Demonstrated executive presence, with the ability to counsel and influence at the most senior levels, collaborate across the business and HR COEs, and communicate exceptionally well
* Proven ability to lead and develop HR professionals, including HR Business Partners, and build a high-performing HR organization
* Experience supporting manufacturing or operations environments, including partnering with plant leadership, managing hourly and salaried workforces, and analyzing labor cost, overtime, absenteeism, and staffing utilization metrics
* Ability to analyze data quickly and provide actionable, strategic business recommendations
* Proven track record of designing and implementing HR strategies that translate organizational strategy into the people agenda and drive measurable business results
* Advanced financial acumen, including the ability to connect people strategy to business financials
* Minimum Bachelor’s degree. MBA or Master’s degree in an HR discipline preferred.
* 15+ years of progressive HR experience, including 7+ years in HR Business Partner or senior HR leadership roles, leading teams and advising executive-level leaders. Health care, pharma, and commercial backgrounds preferred.

We understand compensation is an important factor as you consider the next step in your career. At Vantive, we are committed to equitable pay for all employees, and we strive to be more transparent with our pay practices. The estimated base salary for this position is $180,000 - $250,000 annually. The estimated range is meant to reflect an anticipated salary range for the position. We may pay more or less than the anticipated range based upon market data and other factors, all of which are subject to change. Individual pay is based on upon location, skills and expertise, experience, and other relevant factors. For questions about this, our pay philosophy, and available benefits, please speak to the recruiter if you decide to apply and are selected for an interview.

**US Benefits at Vantive**

This is where your well-being matters. Vantive offers comprehensive compensation and benefits packages for eligible roles. Our health and well-being benefits include medical, dental and vision coverage that start on day one, as well as insurance coverage for basic life, accident, short-term and long-term disability, and business travel accident insurance. Financial and retirement benefits include the Aon Pooled Employer Plan (“Aon PEP”), Vantive’s 401(k) retirement savings plan, to help you prepare for your future. The Aon PEP is designed to help improve retirement outcomes by providing retirement resources more efficiently. The plan offers a robust set of investment options, financial education, and a suite of resources to support your retirement goals.

We also offer Flexible Spending Accounts, educational assistance programs, and time-off benefits such as paid holidays, paid time off ranging from 20 to 35 days based on length of service, family and medical leaves of absence, and paid parental leave. Additional benefits include commuting benefits, the Employee Discount Program, the Employee Assistance Program (EAP), and childcare benefits. Join us and enjoy the competitive compensation and benefits we offer to our employees. For additional information regarding Vantive’s US Benefits, please speak with your recruiter or visit our Benefits site: Benefits | Vantive

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

Vantive is an equal opportunity employer. Vantive evaluates qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, protected veteran status, disability/handicap status or any other legally protected characteristic. 
 
Know Your Rights: Workplace Discrimination is Illegal

**Reasonable Accommodation**

Vantive is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities globally. If, because of a medical condition or disability, you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the application or interview process, please click on the link here and let us know the nature of your request along with your contact information. Form Link

**Recruitment Fraud Notice** 
 
Vantive has discovered incidents of employment scams, where fraudulent parties pose as Vantive employees, recruiters, or other agents, and engage with online job seekers in an attempt to steal personal and/or financial information. To learn how you can protect yourself, review our Recruitment Fraud Notice.

card.title: Plant General Manager
card.description:
At Cavco Industries, Inc. (NASDAQ CVCO), our 7000 team members are at the heart of everything we do. We design and produce quality, affordable factory-built homes. We are also a leading producer of park model RVs, vacation cabins and factory-built commercial structures. In addition to providing competitive pay and benefits, we provide opportunities for development and upward mobility, while investing in the communities we serve. Our values are our foundation. We’re constantly striving to diversify our teams to ensure we have the best and brightest talent. We’re deeply committed to creating an inclusive and equitable workplace where each person can contribute.

 

**ABOUT THE ROLE**

Cavco is seeking an experienced and strategic leader within the manufactured housing industry to oversee and direct overall plant operations. The General Manager is responsible for ensuring business objectives are achieved professionally, ethically, and in accordance with company policy and core values. The General Manager has a responsibility to influence core values by demonstrating them. Safety and Quality will be emphasized as priority over throughput and demonstrated in business planning through measurable annual results. Additionally, the General Manager is responsible for decisions which influence operational results including but not limited to profitability, plant direction, product mix and pricing. The General Manager has the management responsibility and authority for the total operation of an individual plant. He/she is accountable for results, development of KPIs, and continuous improvement. Relocation assistance may be offered for qualified candidates willing to relocate for the role.

 

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES**

The General Manager is responsible for the overall leadership, performance, and compliance of the plant. Duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following:

* **Asset Protection & Controls**
* Ensure all company assets are properly safeguarded and that effective internal controls are established and maintained.
* **Quality Assurance**
* Ensure the plant consistently produces code-compliant, high-quality homes. Conduct periodic inspections of plant output to validate adherence to quality standards.
* **Business Planning & Execution**
* Collaborate with department heads to develop the annual business plan narrative. Ensure operations are aligned with and meet business plan objectives on a daily, weekly, monthly, and annual basis.
* **Regulatory Compliance**
* Maintain full compliance with all local, state, and federal laws and regulations, including those related to product construction, employee health and safety, and recordkeeping.
* **Team Leadership & Development**
* Ensure employees are competent and aligned with company core values. Conduct annual performance reviews for direct reports and administer compensation fairly and equitably based on performance.
* **Customer Engagement**
* Actively cultivate and maintain strong customer relationships. Regularly visit customers to ensure satisfaction and that company operating objectives are being met.
* **Legal & Risk Management**
* Coordinate with the Regional Vice President (RVP) and Cavco Compliance Department regarding any potential or actual legal matters, including service-related issues. Promptly report and forward any legal documents received for proper handling and recordkeeping.
* **Financial Performance & Accountability**
* Review monthly budget versus actual performance with department heads to ensure alignment and maximize profitability. Identify issues, implement corrective actions, and ensure appropriate follow-up.
* **Leadership & Culture**
* Guide, coach, and motivate team members to achieve business plan objectives. Foster a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and high performance.
* **Process Improvement**
* Establish high expectations through strong processes across all areas of management. Focus on improving processes before addressing personnel changes.
* **P&L Management**
* Manage plant profit and loss performance to meet or exceed budget expectations. Understand and optimize the impact of product mix, pricing, and specifications on financial results.
* **Capital Planning**
* Collaborate with department heads to identify capital expenditure needs and develop supporting documentation for investments in systems, equipment, and processes that drive continuous improvement.

 

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in the manufactured housing or related industry required.
* Proven leadership and supervisory experience required.
* Demonstrated ability to lead and support multiple teams in consistently achieving production goals.
* Strong interpersonal and leadership skills, including the ability to support, motivate, and develop team members. Must demonstrate empathy, openness to feedback, and willingness to both provide and receive direction.
* Demonstrated capability to coach and develop people leaders, including functional managers, with a focus on building their ability to lead, coach, and develop their own teams.
* Ability to successfully pass a pre-employment drug screening.
* Demonstrated flexibility and adaptability in a fast-paced, dynamic work environment.

Equal Opportunity Employer 
This employer is required to notify all applicants of their rights pursuant to federal employment laws. For further information, please review the Know Your Rights (https://www.eeoc.gov/poster) notice from the Department of Labor.

card.description:
**Job Description**

**General Summary**
-------------------

The Manufacturing Technical Services Senior Manager provides technical leadership for commercial manufacturing operations for Spray Dried Dispersion (SDD) at external manufacturing partners. The role is accountable for overseeing technical services activities across the commercial manufacturing lifecycle, including manufacturing readiness, process performance, technical investigations, change management, process improvement, and supply-risk mitigation.

The Senior Manager partners with Manufacturing Operations, MS&T, Quality, Supply Chain, Engineering, Regulatory Affairs, and CDMOs/CMOs to ensure manufacturing processes are robust, compliant, reliable, and capable of supporting product supply. The role leads complex cross-functional technical workstreams and develops technical talent within the Manufacturing Technical Services organization.

**Key Duties and Responsibilities**
-----------------------------------

* Lead Manufacturing Technical Services support for assigned commercial manufacturing programs and external manufacturing partners.
* Establish technical plans and priorities to support manufacturing readiness, commercial production campaigns, product supply, and lifecycle-management objectives.
* Provide technical oversight during manufacturing execution; lead escalation and resolution of complex process, equipment, yield, and manufacturing-performance issues.
* Lead technical investigations of significant manufacturing deviations, process excursions, yield loss, equipment failures, and product-quality events; ensure root cause, technical impact, and sustainable corrective actions are clearly defined.
* Oversee manufacturing, process, analytical, and batch-performance trending to identify emerging risks, assess process robustness, and prioritize improvement opportunities.
* Lead technical assessment and approval of change controls, risk assessments, comparability assessments, process updates, and related manufacturing documentation.
* Partner with Manufacturing Operations and Supply Chain to assess technical constraints, manage manufacturing and supply risks, and develop recovery or mitigation plans.
* Lead technical governance with CDMOs/CMOs, including performance review, issue escalation, technical decision-making, data review, and follow-up of technical deliverables.
* Collaborate with MS&T, Quality, Engineering, and Regulatory Affairs to ensure technical strategies align with process-validation requirements, cGMP expectations, regulatory commitments, and product lifecycle plans.
* Lead continuous-improvement initiatives that enhance process robustness, product quality, yield, manufacturing efficiency, and supply reliability.
* Develop, mentor, and provide technical directions to Manufacturing Technical Services staff and matrixed technical teams.
* Travel to support on-site manufacturing activities, CDMO/CMO operations, audits, inspections, and business needs as required (10-20% travel expected)

------------------------

* Deep understanding of pharmaceutical manufacturing processes, testing, controls, and commercial manufacturing operations for Spray Dried Dispersion (SDD)
* Strong knowledge of current Good Manufacturing Practices, pharmaceutical quality systems, and controlled-documentation requirements.
* Demonstrated experience with commercial manufacturing support, technical services, process monitoring, product lifecycle management, and external manufacturing oversight.
* Advanced experience leading complex technical investigations, root-cause analysis, corrective and preventive actions, change controls, risk assessments, and process-improvement initiatives.
* Ability to interpret manufacturing, process, and analytical data; identify process-performance trends; assess technical risks; and recommend practical, sustainable solutions.
* Understanding of manufacturing operations, maintenance, engineering, equipment performance, capacity constraints, and supply-continuity planning.
* Experience leading CDMO/CMO technical relationships, including governance, performance management, technical issue resolution, and escalation.
* Strong cross-functional leadership and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to influence decisions without direct authority.
* Excellent written, verbal, presentation, strategic-thinking, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook, and relevant manufacturing or business systems.

* Bachelor’s degree in Biological Sciences, Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Materials Science, or a related scientific or technical discipline.
* Typically requires 8+ years of experience in biotechnology, pharmaceutical, chemical, or another regulated manufacturing environment, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
* Significant experience supporting commercial manufacturing operations, technical services, MS&T, process development, engineering, quality, or external manufacturing.
* Demonstrated experience leading technical programs, manufacturing workstreams, complex investigations, process improvements, or cross-functional teams.
* Experience working in a cGMP environment and supporting controlled manufacturing documentation is required.
Demonstrate people leadership, matrix leadership, or technical leadership experience is required.

Hybrid-Eligible Or On-Site Eligible

In this Hybrid-Eligible role, you can choose to be designated as:
 
1. **Hybrid** : work remotely up to two days per week; **or select** 
2. **On-Site** : work five days per week on-site with ad hoc flexibility.

Note: The Flex status for this position is subject to Vertex’s Policy on Flex @ Vertex Program and may be changed at any time.

--------------------------------------------

**Location:** Warren, MI 
**Work Model:** On-Site 
**Employment Type:** Full-Time 
**Reports To:**General Manager

**About SLPT**
--------------

**SLPT** is a manufacturing organization committed to delivering quality, reliability, and operational excellence for our customers. Located in Warren, Michigan, we take pride in building a culture where safety, accountability, teamwork, and continuous improvement drive everything we do.Our success starts with our people. We believe the best results come from empowered leaders who are willing to take ownership, develop talent, solve challenges, and continually raise the bar for performance. From the production floor to the leadership team, we foster an environment where employees are respected, supported, and encouraged to grow professionally.As we continue to invest in our operations, technology, and workforce, we are seeking leaders who are passionate about manufacturing excellence and motivated by the opportunity to make a measurable impact. ------------------

* Lead a high-impact manufacturing operation with significant responsibility and visibility.
* Influence plant strategy, operational performance, and business growth.
* Drive Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives that create meaningful results.
* Partner with a collaborative leadership team focused on innovation and operational excellence.
* Develop and mentor employees while building a culture of accountability, engagement, and success.
* Join an organization that values strong leadership, problem-solving, and professional growth.

**At SLPT, you'll have the opportunity to make a lasting impact on our people, our customers, and the future of our manufacturing operations.**

**About the Role**
------------------

Are you a hands-on manufacturing leader who thrives in a fast-paced production environment? We are seeking an experienced **Plant Manager**to lead all aspects of our Warren, Michigan manufacturing operation. In this role, you will oversee safety, quality, production, delivery performance, cost management, and employee development across a 24-hour operation.You will play a key role in driving operational excellence, implementing Lean Manufacturing initiatives, and developing high-performing teams while ensuring customer expectations and business objectives are consistently achieved. The ideal candidate brings strong leadership experience, a passion for continuous improvement, and a proven track record of delivering results in a multi-shift manufacturing environment.

**What You Will Do**
--------------------

* Lead daily manufacturing operations across multiple shifts, ensuring achievement of safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and cost goals.
* Foster a culture of accountability, teamwork, urgency, and continuous improvement throughout the facility.
* Champion a zero-incident safety culture and ensure compliance with OSHA regulations, environmental standards, customer requirements, and company policies.
* Oversee production, maintenance, engineering, quality, materials, warehousing, and logistics functions.
* Drive Lean Manufacturing, Kaizen, and operational excellence initiatives to improve efficiency, reduce waste, and maximize Operational Equipment Effectiveness (OEE).
* Monitor plant financial performance, including labor costs, operating expenses, inventory, maintenance spending, and cost-reduction initiatives.
* Support successful new product launches by partnering with engineering, quality, materials, and program management teams.
* Lead root cause analysis and corrective actions to improve quality performance, reduce scrap and rework, and enhance customer satisfaction.
* Develop leaders and employees through coaching, succession planning, workforce development, and employee engagement initiatives.
* Utilize KPIs and operational metrics to identify opportunities, solve problems, and drive sustainable business improvements.

**What You Bring**
------------------

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field.
* 10+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience.
* 5+ years of experience as a Plant Manager, Operations Manager, or similar senior manufacturing leader.
* Proven success managing multi-shift manufacturing operations.
* Demonstrated ability to achieve and sustain performance targets in safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and cost management.
* Strong financial acumen with experience managing budgets and operational expenses.
* Exceptional leadership, communication, decision-making, and problem-solving skills.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Automotive manufacturing experience.
* Experience supporting or maintaining IATF 16949 and ISO 9001 quality systems.
* Expertise in Lean Manufacturing, Continuous Improvement, Kaizen, and Six Sigma methodologies.
* Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification.
* Certified Manufacturing Manager (CMfgM), PMP certification, or similar professional credentials.
* Master's degree in a related discipline.

Why you'll want to join our team:

* Lead a critical manufacturing operation with broad operational responsibility.
* Make a meaningful impact on plant performance, customer satisfaction, and company growth.
* Partner with an experienced leadership team in a collaborative environment.
* Drive operational excellence and shape the future of the facility.
* Develop and mentor the next generation of manufacturing leaders.
* Influence strategic initiatives, capital investments, and continuous improvement efforts.

**Compensation & Benefits**

Competitive benefits and salary package being offered for this role.

This position is based on-site in Warren, MI and requires a strong presence on the production floor. Occasional travel may be required for customer meetings, supplier visits, training, and corporate initiatives.

**Company Overview**

Delta Galil USA, Inc. is a global manufacturer and marketer of branded and private label apparel products for men, women and children. Since its inception in 1975, the company has continually endeavored to create products that follow a body-before-fabric philosophy, placing equal emphasis on comfort, aesthetics and quality. Delta Galil develops innovative seamless apparel, including bras, shapewear and socks; intimate apparel for women; underwear for men, including under its owned brands Schiesser, Eminence, Organic Basics and Athena; babywear, activewear, sleepwear and loungewear, including under its owned P.J. Salvage and Delta brands. Delta Galil also designs, develops, markets and sells branded denim and apparel under the brand 7 For All Mankind®, and ladies’ and kids’ apparel under the brand Splendid®. In addition, it sells its products under brand names licensed to the company, including adidas, Wolford, Wilson, Columbia, Tommy Hilfiger and others.

**Position Overview**

At Delta Galil, great product only matters if it reaches the shelf at the right cost, at the right quality and on time. As Director, Production & Sourcing, you’ll make that happen. You’ll own Sourcing and Production for your programs, from the first seasonal projection to the moment goods land at our Distribution Center, steering a global network of mills, factories and overseas offices that supply some of the biggest names in mass-market retail.

This is a role with real levers. You’ll negotiate the costs that shape the department’s margin, decide where programs are placed and how capacity is allocated, and lead the cross-functional team through every approval milestone, from BOM handoff to TOP. You’ll partner every day with Design, Planning and our Domestic and Offshore QA teams, and you’ll be the person everyone looks to when a delivery is at risk.

You’ll thrive here if you’re a natural negotiator and a hands-on leader who knows a garment down to its cost components, stays calm when a test fails or a vessel slips, and gets energy from turning a complex calendar into on-time deliveries.

**Key Responsibilities**

Sourcing, Costing & Vendor Strategy

* Share seasonal projections with mills and factories early, locking in key delivery dates and a generic TNA well ahead of order placement.
* Lead program-level cost negotiations that drive best costs and help the department meet or beat seasonal margin goals.
* Build and grow a strong vendor matrix that supports the business’s long-term needs.
* Place programs with overseas mills, factories and offices on time, with program-specific TNAs, the right capacity allocation and production plans that hit contracted deliveries.

Production Execution & Approvals

* Lead the cross-functional team through program TNAs, driving approvals from completed BOM handoff through color and components, fit, pre-production, testing and TOP.
* Work with stakeholders to resolve approval issues and testing failures quickly, escalating to leadership when needed.
* Assess production issues for delivery impact and lead cross-functional decisions on quality levels and ship-mode changes to protect customer deliveries.

Planning, Capacity & Delivery

* Partner with the Planning team to support the business at the right stock levels.
* Own and communicate monthly program capacity plans to mills and factories, flagging loading or capacity risks early.
* Keep POs current in the system, hold factories to timely bookings and approve vessel schedules that line up with customer deliveries.
* Build and maintain delivery reports for weekly team review.

Quality & Continuous Improvement

* Partner with Domestic and Offshore QA, sharing planned program allocation before placement.
* Champion critical QA steps before, during and at the end of production so product arrives at the Distribution Center free of quality issues and every customer order ships on time.
* Work with management to improve process flow and roll out new initiatives.

 
Requirements: 
 

* Minimum years of apparel experience across Product Development, Production, QA and Testing.
* Experience supplying a big-box, mass-market retailer such as Target or Walmart.
* Cut-and-sew knits experience (activewear strongly preferred).
* Deep knowledge of manufacturing, testing and quality control, including fabrics, trims and garment cost components (YY, CM, AU).
* A proven team leader with exceptional negotiation and problem-solving skills with factories and material suppliers.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to connect with factories, suppliers and internal teams at every level.
* Highly organized and detail-oriented, with strong follow-up, a sense of urgency and the ability to juggle multiple projects and teams.
* Advanced Excel skills (VLOOKUPs, pivot tables) and proficiency in Word and Outlook.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Activewear, intimates, loungewear, or knits experience.
* CPM and SMV knowledge, with a thorough understanding of cost component breakdowns.
* Experience traveling overseas to mills and factories.

**This is a hybrid role, with 4 days in our NJ office.**

**PAY RATE: $150,000/yr-$170,000/yr**

At Delta Galil, we strive to hire and nurture amazing talent. Actual salaries will vary depending on factors including but not limited to experience, specialized skills, and internal alignment.

DIVERSITY VISION STATEMENT:

We are committed to creating an inclusive environment that welcomes and values the differences among all of our associates, customers, suppliers, and the communities in which we live and conduct business. We are an equal employment opportunity for minorities, females, protected veterans, and the disabled.

We are committed to providing equal opportunities in employment and treating our associates and applicants without discrimination based on their race, color, gender, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, citizenship, disability, protected veteran status, or any other legally protected factor.

 
Hybrid position:
 
Hybrid 
 
Company Benefits: 
 

As a Delta Galil Associate, you’ll be part of a global fashion company that values innovation, craftsmanship, and people. We’re committed to offering comprehensive and competitive benefits that reflect our culture of care, creativity, and collaboration — but most importantly, benefits that fit you.

Our diverse range of programs is designed to support your total well-being — empowering you to make the best choices for yourself, your loved ones, and your lifestyle.

Below are a few of the benefits available to our Associates:

* Multi-brand merchandise discount, including Splendid, 7 For All Mankind, and PJ Salvage
* Comprehensive Health Coverage: Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance, as well as Basic Life/Voluntary Life/Disability/Critical Illness
* Financial Wellness: 401(k) Retirement Program with Company match and 529 College Savings Plan, as well as Tax-Advantage Health & Transit Accounts
* Personal and sick time off, vacation time, floating days, and company-observed holidays
* Paid Volunteer Time Off to dedicate your skills and time towards charitable activities
* From weekly breakfasts and monthly milestone celebrations to leadership-led panels, and, team-building events, we offer plenty of fun ways to connect—both in person and virtually

card.title: Manufacturing Quality Senior Manager
card.description:
**Job Description**
The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Quality builds and leads the quality system supporting Harris' manufacturing network. This role owns quality and certifications across multiple facilities, including the ISO 9001 and ASME (non-nuclear) certification programs, inspection and hold/release, and independent verification of VDC deliverables, so products leave Harris' shops conforming to customer, code, and specification requirements.
 
 
This role builds and leads the plant-level QA/QC team, who will report directly to it. It holds quality stop-work authority and provides independent verification across facilities. The Senior Manager partners with the Harris corporate QA/QC program, applying and extending it to manufacturing, and works with Manufacturing Operations, Engineering and VDC, Supply Chain, Industrial Engineering, and Safety. The role standardizes quality practices and supports certification of new facilities as the network scales.
 
 
**Core Responsibilities**
**Quality Management System & Certifications**

* Own the manufacturing certification programs, including ISO 9001 and ASME, with documentation, internal audits, and management review.
* Lead certification and recertification for new and existing facilities, including customer and third-party audits.
* Align manufacturing procedures with the Harris corporate QMS manual and manage manufacturing-specific procedures and records.
* Drive consistent quality system implementation across the network.
* Represent Harris in professional and industry organizations.

**Plant QA/QC Leadership & Inspection**

* Build, staff, and lead the plant-level QA/QC team, including roles, hiring, training, and standards.
* Establish and own inspection, verification, and hold/release processes, from receiving through final inspection.
* Define inspection plans and travelers by product and customer requirement.
* Ensure welding procedures and welder qualifications meet code, and manage calibration of inspection equipment.
* Manage third-party inspection firms and their scope, schedule, and results

**VDC Deliverable QA/QC Review**

* Spot-check VDC deliverables, including drawings, models, and BOMs, before they reach the shop, as an independent check on VDC's own QA/QC.
* Audit VDC's QA/QC process and record results, and raise gaps with VDC leadership.
* Track shop-found drawing, model, and BOM issues, and feed trends back to VDC and Engineering.
* Hold deliverables that fail verification until corrected.

**Nonconformance, Corrective Action & Quality Performance**

* Own the nonconformance (NCR) process, root cause analysis, and corrective and preventive actions, including supplier issues.
* Track and report quality metrics, including rework, weld repair, NCR trends, and customer complaints.
* Work with Industrial Engineering and plant leadership to turn quality data into improvements.

**Quality Stop-Work Authority**

* Exercise stop-work authority when product, process, or documentation does not meet requirements, escalating to the SVP as needed.
* Define clear criteria for stop, hold, and release.

**Production Readiness & Supplier Quality**

* Set quality requirements, inspection and test plans, and documentation for new products and projects at the production readiness gate and manage 3rd party inspection companies.
* Partner with Supply Chain on supplier quality, receiving inspection, and material certifications.
* Support customer quality requirements and audits for external customers.

**Cross-Functional Collaboration**
**This Role Works Closely With**

* Harris corporate QA/QC program leadership
* Manufacturing Operations, Industrial Engineering, Safety
* Engineering, VDC, and Product Engineering
* Supply Chain, Purchasing, and Fulfillment & Logistics
* Manufacturing Business Development and Estimating
* Customers, auditors, and certification bodies

The Senior Manager owns the manufacturing quality system and independent verification. Plant leadership owns producing quality product in the shop.
 
 
**Required Qualifications**

* Experience building and leading quality assurance or quality control across multiple manufacturing, fabrication, or prefabrication facilities, including hiring and developing quality staff.
* Experience leading ISO 9001 and ASME or other code-based certification and recertification, including internal audits and corrective action.
* Experience with inspection, nonconformance management, and root cause analysis.
* Ability to read engineering drawings, specifications, and codes.
* Ability to hold plant leaders accountable while keeping production moving.
* Strong communication skills with customers, auditors, and cross-functional teams.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with nuclear quality assurance, ASME boiler and pressure vessel code, or other code-based quality programs.
* Professional Engineer (PE) license.
* Experience with welding, piping, structural, or modular MEP fabrication.
* Certifications such as CWI, ASQ CQE/CQA/CMQ, or Lead Auditor.
* Experience with quality and production tracking systems such as STRATUS.

**This Role Is**
**What This Role Is (and Is Not)**

* The enterprise owner of the manufacturing quality system and certifications.
* The builder and leader of plant-level QA/QC across facilities.
* The authority for inspection, hold/release, and quality stop-work.
* An independent check that protects customers and Harris' reputation as the network scales.

**This Role Is NOT**

* The owner of plant production or shop-floor output (Manufacturing Operations).
* The owner of the Harris corporate QA/QC program.
* The owner of VDC's internal QA/QC (VDC).
* Responsible for safety programs or safety stop-work (Safety).
* The owner of product design or productization (Product Engineering).

**Your life at Harris**
As one of the country's leading mechanical contractors, Harris offers you the best of both worlds: the stability, resources and opportunities of a national company, and the team culture, creative spirit and customer loyalty of a local business. If you thrive on variety and new challenges, we want to meet you!
 
 
From stadiums to manufacturing facilities, power plants to hospitals, concert halls to classrooms, we handle projects of all sizes and complexity from multiple regional locations across the country.
 
 
**Harris Benefits + Compensation**

* Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance
* 401K with company match
* Vacation time, sick time, and paid holidays
* Paid Parental leave
* Short-Term Incentive Plan

Visit our Careers Page for additional benefit details: https://www.harriscompany.com/careers/employee-benefits-at-a-glance
 
 
**Pay Range**
$111,060.64 - $166,590.97
 
 
The actual salary offer will vary by candidate based on a wide range of factors such as specific skills, qualifications, experience, and location.
 
 
Equal Opportunity Employer/Protected Veterans/Individuals with Disabilities
 
 
This employer is required to notify all applicants of their rights pursuant to federal employment laws. For further information, please review the Know Your Rights notice from the Department of Labor.
